tasks.short: Consult production staff about lighting requirements.

steps.what: Locate and read the current lighting brief, production plan and venue constraints
inputs: actual production request
current production brief and venue information
outputs: located and understood current lighting sources

steps.what: Consult lighting director and production staff to determine actual lighting requirements
inputs: located and understood current lighting sources
actual director and production preferences
outputs: actual agreed lighting requirements and unresolved questions

steps.what: Write and check actual lighting requirements and retain the internal consultation record
inputs: actual agreed lighting requirements and unresolved questions

tasks.design: Configure current production-brief links in {DOCS}/{PROJECT}. Reduce repeated version navigation while retaining consultation, requirements judgement and the full written requirements record with its ordinary ungated save.
tasks.previous_blocker: The current brief and venue constraints may be scattered.
tasks.enabler_now: Native project-to-document links can remove some locating work.
tasks.still_hard: Lighting intent and practical production tradeoffs need conversation.
tasks.human_edge: The technician identifies a requested look that conflicts with the actual venue.
tasks.altitude: Slightly less brief navigation; lighting decisions stay unchanged.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: current project-document links can reduce locating lighting briefs without replacing production consultation.

assumptions: Provisional shares: three of15 source points are repeated locating/version navigation; source reading, consultation and written requirements stay. No free transcript and no saving for ordinary internal save.

Production owner supplies brief id/revision, scene or event identity and venue link. Missing sources are obtained manually. Technician creates actual requirements only after consultation. Boundary is live consultation and its actual internal record, without an assumed second email delivery.
unknowns: Are current briefs already linked from the production job?
research_questions: Can current links prevent preparation from an obsolete lighting brief?

incremental.description: Maintain current production brief and venue links.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: High removes3 locating points minus0.3 upkeep=2.7. Low: a new production arrives with largely unindexed material, leaving only1 venue-link locating point removed, minus0.3=0.7. Actual reading, consultation and written requirements keep their time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Notify supervisors about needed major lighting repairs.

steps.what: Assess actual lighting equipment fault and establish why a major repair is needed
inputs: actual faulty lighting equipment
actual observed symptoms and safe inspection conditions
outputs: actual verified fault observations and repair concern

steps.what: Locate actual equipment identity, maintenance history and applicable repair contact
inputs: actual verified fault observations and repair concern
actual equipment maintenance records
outputs: checked equipment identity and repair history context

steps.what: Notify supervisor in a live call about actual fault, repair need and urgency
inputs: actual verified fault observations and repair concern
checked equipment identity and repair history context

steps.what: Record and check actual fault and supervisor response in assigned maintenance notes
inputs: actual supervisor notification and response
actual verified fault observations and repair concern

tasks.design: Configure equipment-identity links to history and repair contacts in maintenance {OPS_SYSTEM}. Keep physical fault assessment, live supervisor notification and actual assigned maintenance notes human; do not invent an additional written send or self-approval job.
tasks.previous_blocker: Equipment and repair history can take several screens to locate.
tasks.enabler_now: Native asset views can remove repeated navigation.
tasks.still_hard: Repair severity and urgency depend on actual equipment condition.
tasks.human_edge: The technician explains why a fault must interrupt production.
tasks.altitude: Less history navigation; repair judgement and notification stay unchanged.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: native maintenance asset views can reduce locating repair context while fault assessment and live notification remain human.

assumptions: Provisional live-notification route: s3 is the actual conversation, not a hidden machine message send. Separate actual notes5 retain full writing/check/save time. If the real route uses a written notification, map its actual final review and separate send instead; no send saving is claimed here.

Maintenance owner supplies asset id, serial/model, dated repair history and actual supervisor/repair contact. Technician supplies real symptoms and urgency; no fault or completed repair inferred from history. Three of15 lookup points are repeated navigation. Existing views get no new saving.
unknowns: Does this technician own maintenance notes and use a live notification route?
research_questions: Can the asset view locate the right repair contact without hiding unresolved faults?

incremental.description: Maintain equipment-history links and current repair contacts.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: High removes3 equipment-history navigation points minus0.3 upkeep=2.7. Low: an unregistered hired fixture needs manual repair-history inquiry, leaving only0.5 contact-navigation points removed, minus0.3=0.2. Fault assessment, supervisor conversation and actual record stay unchanged.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Program lighting consoles and load lighting-control programs.

steps.what: Determine actual fixture patch, cue intent and console programming requirements
inputs: actual director's lighting requirements
actual fixture inventory and verified patch

steps.what: Program fixture groups, palettes and cue values in the lighting console workspace
inputs: chosen fixture/cue programming specification
actual reusable fixture groups and palettes

steps.what: Check complete staged console program against actual patch, cue intent and preview
inputs: staged lighting console program
chosen fixture/cue programming specification
outputs: checked final staged console program and target console identity

steps.what: Review final staged program and authorise its loading on the specified production console
inputs: checked final staged console program and target console identity
outputs: independently authorised final program version and target console

steps.what: Load the authorised exact program onto the specified production lighting console
inputs: independently authorised final program version and target console
outputs: actual loaded console program and load status

tasks.design: Test native fixture-group and palette reuse in the lighting-console {OPS_SYSTEM}. Remove only repeated entry covered by those presets; retain patch decisions, complete preview checks, the existing director review and the exact production-console load as its own action with no saving.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated group and palette values are entered for similar lighting setups.
tasks.enabler_now: Native reusable console elements can remove repeated entry without inventing cues.
tasks.still_hard: Patch accuracy, actual lighting intent and safe live behaviour need people.
tasks.human_edge: The technician catches a reused palette that points an actual fixture incorrectly.
tasks.altitude: Less repeated cue entry; lighting intent and live-control authority stay unchanged.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: lighting-console groups and palettes can reuse fixture settings while cue intent and live loading require human checking.

assumptions: Provisional production route with an existing independent lighting director review5, excluded from focal baseline95; no new approval ceremony. Eight of40 entry points are repeated group/palette entry. Existing console automation/runtime receives no credit.

Production owner supplies actual cue intent; technician verifies fixture id, universe/address, mode, group, palette values and target console/version. Missing or changed fixture modes require manual programming and preview, not guessed mappings. Ordinary workspace saves are included unchanged in retained programming/checking; s5 is actual production-console loading, priced at1 point with no saving.
unknowns: Which fixture groups and palettes are already reused?
What existing review authorises the actual production load?
research_questions: Can presets remove repeated entry while a preview catches every changed fixture mapping?

incremental.description: Maintain verified fixture groups/palettes and preview changed mappings.

approvals.approved_version: s3 exact checked final program snapshot and named target console reviewed in s4; any change voids approval

Low: a touring rig changes most fixture modes, leaving only3 unchanged group-entry points removable, giving3/95*100 minus1=2.157. Patch choices, full checks, director review and the1-point production load retain their time.

tasks.short: Visit locations and assess structural and electrical layout before lighting setup.

steps.what: Locate current location drawings, electrical layout and documented rigging constraints
inputs: actual production location
actual venue drawings and equipment requirements

steps.what: Visit and assess actual structural and electrical layout and lighting setup constraints
inputs: located current venue source set
actual location condition and access
outputs: actual structural/electrical observations and unresolved constraints

steps.what: Write and check actual location assessment findings and retain the internal survey record
inputs: actual structural/electrical observations and unresolved constraints
located current venue source set

tasks.design: Configure actual venue-to-drawing links in {DOCS}/{PROJECT}. Save repeated source navigation while keeping the physical visit, structural/electrical assessment and complete written findings unchanged; an old drawing never substitutes for current site conditions.
tasks.previous_blocker: Venue source revisions can be difficult to locate.
tasks.enabler_now: Native project links can expose the current supplied source set.
tasks.still_hard: Actual support, access and electrical conditions require site assessment and qualified escalation.
tasks.human_edge: The technician identifies a site condition that makes the drawing unsafe to rely on.
tasks.altitude: Less drawing navigation; site assessment remains human.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: venue drawing links can reduce source navigation while structural and electrical site assessment needs real observation.

assumptions: Provisional source20 has three repeated locating points removed; actual drawing reading remains. Site observations and assigned written assessment are separate and fully retained, including ordinary ungated save. No setup, engineering certification or external report is invented.

Venue owners supply actual location id, drawing revision/date, electrical distribution and documented support constraints. Missing capacities or inconsistent drawings require manual owner/qualified-engineer confirmation; no capacity is inferred from an image. Technician supplies fresh site findings after the visit. Existing links earn no new saving.
unknowns: Does the venue provide current usable drawings?
research_questions: Can source links distinguish documented limits from unverified site assumptions?

incremental.description: Maintain venue-source revisions and applicability links.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: High removes3 drawing-navigation points minus0.4 upkeep=2.6. Low: a new venue has incomplete drawings needing manual inquiry, leaving only0.5 known location-source points removed, minus0.4=0.1. Visit, actual assessment and full written findings retain their time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional
